status: Eight real local-Linux kernel component cases pass for unchanged fixed ARP helper source, including foreign preexisting/replacement retention, cleanup refusal and restart admission, keeper death, and both-owner crash recovery. Unsafe foreign-delete mutant is rejected. This does not qualify the on-radio final graph, Linux2.6 or concurrent administrator writes between lookup and deletion.

mutation.change: Separate mutant removes only restore() refusal for a nonmatching neighbor; production binary/source remain unchanged.

original_fixture_failure.cause: Real Linux purges neighbors when interface MAC changes; the first fixture incorrectly assumed retention. Corrected fixture establishes a replacement after the MAC change and confirms helper refusal with retained intent. Each keeper also receives its own process group for one-syscall both-owner death.

scope_limits: Actual ioctl/kernel neighbors and process death are exercised on the local x86_64 Linux kernel in user/net/mount/PID namespaces. The compiled C source matches current83d6; it is not the ARM64 or ARMv7 ELF and is not executing on either radio.

The namespace begins with loopback only, no main route and mapped subordinate IDs. It contains one dummyeth0.10 and a private chroot/tmpfs journal/proc mount. No real NIC, remote socket, radio, RF or host-root operation is used.
The initial fixture failure remains false; its kernel-behavior correction changes no production code or admission policy.

The existing read/check/delete sequence is not an atomic compare-and-swap against an unrelated administrator write. These cases replace state before cleanup, not in the lookup/delete interval. Arbitrary concurrent administrator changes remain outside the proved scope.

The on-radio final process graph, GUI terminal state and explicit recovery under a conflicting ARP replacement remain separate open P5 qualification. The pending one5W DSP API-loss follow-up has not been dispatched or approved by this local test.
Actual6300 profile, Linux2.6 kernel, one-core scheduling, disk and RF qualification remain open; no8600 hard-coded profile is silently applied to6300.
Full P1-P10, unresolved natural128/cold bypass, other fault/credential/stale-cache scopes, repeated/raw/extended RF, final integrated stock comparison and independent release gates remain active.
